facts.text: Local newspapers print school sports results and town council meeting notices.
Families still receive printed television schedules with some newspapers.
A radio host announces road closures between songs during the morning commute.
Drivers tune into local radio for weather warnings during severe storms.
High school students follow local sports scores through newspaper websites.
Some residents write letters to the editor about neighborhood concerns.
A community bulletin board displays flyers for concerts and charity events.
The public library lends printed novels alongside electronic books.
Some readers borrow electronic books through the public library website.
A magazine rack stands near the checkout counter at the grocery store.
Teenagers discuss short online videos shared among classmates.
A local theater advertises showtimes on its website and entrance marquee.
Some families rent films on discs from automated kiosks outside stores.
A household keeps a collection of film discs on a living room shelf.
A music fan buys a compact disc at a secondhand shop.
Some listeners buy digital music files to keep on portable players.
Teenagers make playlists for school dances using digital music libraries.
A small-town radio station broadcasts announcements for weekend fundraisers.
Some residents subscribe to a printed weekly newspaper for local coverage.
A television news crew interviews residents after a damaging storm.
Friends discuss a televised competition the morning after its broadcast.
Sports fans gather at a diner to watch a game on television.
A printed community calendar lists performances at the school auditorium.
Some local reporters post breaking updates before the next printed edition.
Residents share photographs of a town parade through online community pages.
A caller leaves a voicemail when the local radio contest line is busy.
